answer.why_different: The generated document adds a callback structure at the operation level, treating the notification target as a callback keyed by the request-body runtime expression. This is a different structure/address from the official document, which has no such callback, and the generated callback is reported as invalid OpenAPI 3.0 because the required `$ref` is missing.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification defines `{notificationTarget}` as a separate resource receiving HTTP POST notifications, with notification request bodies and 204, 4xx, and 5xx responses. The evidence does not establish that this resource should be represented as a callback under `PUT /{className}={id}`.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 permits callback keys expressed as runtime expressions, and a callback value is a Path Item Object. However, the supplied validation result explicitly reports this generated callback as invalid because `$ref` is required, so the generated structure cannot be accepted as a valid OpenAPI 3.0 callback in this document.
answer.clearer_why: The official side has no misleading or invalid callback declaration. The generated side introduces an invalid callback structure and may incorrectly associate the notification target with the PUT operation.

citations.quote: {expression} | [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) | A Path Item Object used to define a callback request and expected responses.

differences.reason: The generated side adds a callback that is absent from the official document and is explicitly reported as invalid OpenAPI 3.0 because `$ref` is required. Although the specification defines POST behavior for the separate `{notificationTarget}` resource, it does not support adding this callback under the PUT operation; see C1, S1, and O4.

#### Callback Object  
A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.
Each value in the map is a [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) that describes a set of requests that may be initiated by the API provider and the expected responses.
The key value used to identify the callback object is an expression, evaluated at runtime, that identifies a URL to use for the callback operation.  
##### Patterned Fields
Field Pattern | Type | Description
---|:---:|---

operationRef: 'https://na2.gigantic-server.com/#/paths/~12.0~1repositories~1{username}/get'
parameters:
username: $response.body#/username
```  
Note that in the use of `operationRef`, the _escaped forward-slash_ is necessary when
using JSON references.  
##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name

evidence.query: callback runtime expression URL of the notification request body $request.body#/notificationTarget
evidence.title: Examples
evidence.text:
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
